text:
sam: Heads up — I spotted a runtime guide snippet that still shows batch_size: 64 for continuous batching. Customers on the new kernel reported OOMs. Path: /docs/runtime/continuous-batching.md

tara: Ugh, thanks for flagging. Do we have an owner for that page? I can do a tiny PR to lower the default if no one else picks it up.

sam: I think it used to be under eng-runtime docs ownership but not sure who is owning those pages now. @ankur usually knows kernel defaults.

devex: I can take this and open a quick PR to change example + add a short note about kernel differences. Will ping runtime for confirmation.

ankur: Confirmed — the newer nv12 kernel path reduced safe default to 32 in our runtime because of buffer allocations. Lowering the example from 64 -> 32 is correct. Also good to add a short callout: "kernel-sensitive default — bump carefully, test on target hardware."

sam: Thanks. Could we also add a tiny troubleshooting bullet in the runbook that points to the OOM log snippet so support can triage faster?

devex: Yep. Plan: 1) PR to docs: example change + callout. 2) add runbook bullet + example OOM grep. 3) ask L10n to backport to ja/es if merged. I'll open PR in ~15m.

deploy-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4123 — title: "runtime: reduce continuous-batching example default to 32 + note" (CI queued) :shipit:

tara: Nice. I'll review once CI passes. If green, I'll merge and request a tiny ops-cherry-pick to the runbook repo.

ankur: Quick check from runtime side: also add a one-liner about KV-cache growth affecting memory at long context lengths. Otherwise LGTM.

devex: Added that line to the PR description and file. Also included sample grep for logs:
```
grep -E "(OOM|MallocFailed|out of memory)" /var/log/redwood/runtime/*.log | tail -n 50
```

sam: Sweet. Leaving here for the docs queue — thanks team.

tara: FYI — pinging @l10n-team in case backports need triage after merge. :wave:
